info.title: nof1-causal-lab episode API
info.description:
The episode machine is the single interface to an N-of-1 causal analysis. An
external agent drives it entirely over this HTTP API — the same surface the web
viewer uses. There is no SDK and no MCP server: `curl` is the interface.

## Orientation

Call `GET /api/machine` once. It returns the static artifact graph — every
transition with what it consumes, produces, and optionally co-produces — plus
each transition's creation class and the derivation graph:

- `deterministic` — pure compute, no credentials (e.g. identification).
- `batch_llm` — bulk LLM compute on the service's ambient key. You trigger it
  with a `run` move; you never supply a key.
- `judgment` — proposal work you can do yourself by writing the produced
  artifact directly. These transitions are flagged `writable`.

## The loop

1. `GET /api/machine` once, then `GET /api/episodes/{workspace_id}` for the live
   state: per-artifact freshness, the legal moves, and whether an auto-run is
   active.
2. Propose a move at `POST /api/episodes/{workspace_id}/moves` — either
   `{"move": {"kind": "run", "artifact_id": "latent_structure"}}` to run a transition, or
   `{"move": {"kind": "write", "artifact_id": "latent_structure", "provenance": "llm"}, "payload": {...}}`
   to author a judgment artifact directly.
3. Long transitions (`statistical_model_spec`, `posterior` — minutes to hours) can outlive a client
   timeout. Prefer `POST /api/episodes/{workspace_id}/auto` (a background driver
   that runs enabled transitions in dependency order) and poll the state.
4. Read what happened at `GET /api/episodes/{workspace_id}/timeline`: `applied`,
   `rejected` (illegal, state unchanged), or `raised` (typed transition error).

## Staleness

A `write` becomes a new provenance root and marks everything downstream stale
until re-run. Numeric tools (`simulate`, `get_model_info`) hard-flag
stale provenance chains in their warnings — never report numbers past those
flags.

## Data in, results out

Upload raw data at `POST /api/upload` (`multipart/form-data` with `workspaceId`
and `file`) before running the `raw_data` transition. Read artifact payloads at
`GET /api/episodes/{workspace_id}/artifacts/{artifact_id}`; binary files
(parquet, pickle) are served individually from `.../files/{filename}`.

## Read-only deployments

The hosted viewer's backend serves these same read endpoints against a published
store with no move plane. `GET /api/capabilities` reports `moves_enabled`; every
move returns 403 when it is `false`.

get.description:
Current episode state: the single read to poll while navigating.

Returns per-artifact freshness (existence, staleness, version, provenance),
the `legal` moves available right now, and `auto_running` — whether the
background driver is active. Replayed from the append-only transition log,
so it works even against a published read-only store.

Batch canonical aggregates in one committed read transaction.

Omit `at_seq` for the latest applied move, or select a committed journal sequence.
Zero selects the empty model. Rejected/raised attempts are not revisions (404).
Use the returned `seq` for subsequent aggregate or collection reads at the same revision.
Canonical latent structure, including its default outcome, at the selected revision.

get.description: One display projection from the selected committed model revision.

The transition journal: every move attempt in order.

Each record is `applied` (state advanced), `rejected` (illegal move, state
unchanged), or `raised` (the transition ran but threw — the record carries the
typed error). Re-running after a `raised`/`rejected` is just proposing the
move again.

Fine-grained telemetry (e.g. extraction worker fan-out, transition progress).

Pass the last-seen event id as `after` to page forward; omit it for the full
stream. This is finer-grained than the timeline, which records only whole
move outcomes.

One artifact version: meta + inline JSON payloads.

Defaults to the episode's *current* version from replayed applied transition
effects. Binary payload files (parquet, pickle) are listed by name, never
inlined.

Traces of the applied transition that produced an artifact version.

Defaults to the episode's current version. The join runs over the
transition journal, so it works against a published read-only store.
One promoted LLM trace from ``episode/traces/{seq:06d}/{subroutine_id}.json``.

One declared payload file from an artifact version.

Defaults to the episode's current version. Unlike the JSON artifact
endpoint, this serves binary files as bytes and refuses undeclared
filenames so callers cannot browse arbitrary workspace paths.

post.description:
Ensure the episode workflow exists; optionally seed the `question` root.

Idempotent: attaches to an existing episode or starts a fresh one. Passing
`question` writes the `question` root artifact with `human` provenance.
Upload raw data at `POST /api/upload` before running the `raw_data`
transition. Returns the same shape as
`GET /api/episodes/{id}`.

Propose one move; blocks until it is applied, rejected, or raises.

Two kinds:

- Run a transition: `{"move": {"kind": "run", "artifact_id": "latent_structure"}}`.
- Author a judgment artifact directly (skip the in-service stage):
  `{"move": {"kind": "write", "artifact_id": "latent_structure", "provenance":
  "llm"}, "payload": {...}}`. The payload is schema-validated against that
  artifact's contract, journaled, and provenance-stamped; the write becomes a
  new provenance root and marks everything downstream stale until re-run.

The synchronous outcome is the same record the timeline stores. Long transitions
(statistical model specification, posterior — minutes to hours) can outlive a client timeout; for
those prefer `POST /api/episodes/{workspace_id}/auto` plus polling.

Start the default navigation policy in the background.

Runs enabled stages in dependency order while their outputs are missing or
stale, stopping when quiescent or when a move fails. Returns immediately;
follow progress with `GET /api/episodes/{workspace_id}` (`auto_running`) and
the timeline. An LLM navigator replaces this policy by proposing `moves`
itself. 409 if a driver is already active for this workspace.

get.description:
Whether this deployment serves the move plane.

`moves_enabled` is `false` on the hosted read-only viewer backend, where
every `POST` (moves, auto-run, start-episode) returns 403 and only the read
endpoints are live.
Published/local workspaces visible through this facade.

post.description: Stage one raw input file for the raw_data transition.

get.description:
The static artifact graph and action hierarchy — read once to orient.

Each transition entry declares what it `consumes`, `produces`, and
optionally co-produces (`produces_optional`), plus its **creation
class**: `deterministic` (pure compute, no credentials), `batch_llm` (bulk
LLM compute on the service's ambient key — you trigger it with a `run` move,
you never supply a key), or `judgment` (proposal work you can author yourself
by writing the produced artifact directly — these are flagged `writable`).

List a context's validation/query tools — the same tools the in-service LLM loops use.

Each entry is `{name, description, parameters, result}` where `parameters`
and `result` are JSON Schemas. Fetch this first to learn a tool's argument
shape, then call `POST /api/tools/{context_id}/{tool_name}`. Examples:
ranking `simulate` / `get_model_info`, statistical-model-spec `search_literature`.

schema.title: Response Get Tool Schemas Api Tools  Context Id  Get

post.description:
Execute a context tool against the workspace's current artifact-store versions.

Body is `{"workspace_id": "...", "input": {...}}` where `input` matches the
tool's `parameters` schema from `GET /api/tools/{context_id}`; 422 on a schema
violation. Numeric tools hard-flag stale provenance chains in their result
warnings — do not report numbers past those flags.

ArtifactRef.title: ArtifactRef
ArtifactRef.description: An artifact reference identifies the exact stored version that supports a model fact.

ArtifactVersionInfo.title: ArtifactVersionInfo
ArtifactVersionInfo.description:
Artifact version metadata records how a stored artifact was produced and which inputs it
used.

``derived_from`` pins the exact input versions the payload was computed
from. For root artifacts (user writes) it is empty. ``created_at`` is
stamped by the activity that produced the version — never inside workflow
code, where wall-clock time is non-deterministic.

construct_polarity.description: Whether higher indicator values move in the same direction as the construct (`positive`) or the opposite direction (`negative`).

aggregation.description: Aggregation function applied when bucketing raw extractions within the indicator support window. Measurement-structure support is currently limited to: first, last, sum, count, mean, std. Available parser operators: count, cv, entropy, first, instability, iqr, kurtosis, last, max, mean, median, min, n_unique, p10, p25, p75, p90, p99, range, skew, std, sum, trend, var

observation_window.title: Observation Window
observation_window.description: Optional duration string describing the support window summarized by this indicator (for example '1mo' for a monthly average on a daily model clock). If omitted, the support window defaults to the global model_clock.

ordinal_levels.title: Ordinal Levels
ordinal_levels.description: Ordered list of level labels from lowest to highest for ordinal indicators (e.g., ['low', 'medium', 'high']). Required when measurement_dtype='ordinal' to ensure correct numeric encoding.

categorical_levels.title: Categorical Levels
categorical_levels.description: Exhaustive list of level labels for categorical indicators (e.g., ['home', 'work', 'other']). Required when measurement_dtype='categorical' to ensure correct numeric encoding.

source_columns.title: Source Columns
source_columns.description: Raw data column names referenced by how_to_measure. Used to project chunks to only relevant columns before extraction.

computed_rule.description: Optional deterministic support-window expression for extraction_mode='computed'. Use this when a computed indicator needs formulas, thresholds, or multiple source columns instead of a direct single-column aggregation. The expression must return one scalar per support window.

extraction_mode.title: Extraction Mode
extraction_mode.description: 'computed' (deterministic pipeline extraction) or 'semantic' (LLM extraction). Use 'computed' when the indicator can be derived deterministically either from a direct source-column aggregation or from a computed_rule support-window expression over the declared source_columns.

for interpolation. PSIS reliability is assessed with Pareto-k diagnostics.

SMC diagnostics track particle sampling through its tempering schedule, effective sample
sizes, and acceptance rates.

SavedScenario.title: SavedScenario
SavedScenario.description: A saved scenario preserves a labeled causal query and its optional narrative summary.

SavedScenariosArtifact.title: SavedScenariosArtifact
SavedScenariosArtifact.description: Saved scenarios preserve the selected queries for a fitted model.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: How the clamped value is specified over the window.

value.title: Value
value.description: Required when mode='set'. Absolute latent-space value.

amount.title: Amount
amount.description: Required when mode='shift'. Additive delta from the start-state value.

value_start.title: Value Start
value_start.description: Required when mode='ramp'. Value at from_day.

value_end.title: Value End
value_end.description: Required when mode='ramp'. Value at to_day.

values.title: Values
values.description: Required when mode='trajectory'. Values sampled evenly across the window.

from_day.title: From Day
from_day.description: Window onset in days from the rollout start.

to_day.title: To Day
to_day.description: Window end in days from the rollout start. Null runs through the horizon.

ScenarioClamp.title: ScenarioClamp
ScenarioClamp.description: A resolved clamp binds its transport label to a persistent construct identity.

ScenarioEvaluation.title: ScenarioEvaluation
ScenarioEvaluation.description: An evaluation binds a scientific query to one model and exact posterior version.

ScenarioEvaluationResult.title: ScenarioEvaluationResult
ScenarioEvaluationResult.description: One posterior-specific evaluation and its matching computed outputs.

ScenarioQuery.title: ScenarioQuery
ScenarioQuery.description: A scientific query keeps its identity across model and posterior revisions.

estimand.title: Estimand
estimand.description: Report the final-horizon outcome effect or the full effect trajectory.

horizon_days.title: Horizon Days
horizon_days.description: Forward horizon in days from the rollout start.

projection.title: Projection
projection.description: Report latent outcome effects, manifest projections, or both.

outcome_label.title: Outcome Label
outcome_label.description: Display name of the query's outcome at execution time.

reference_mean.title: Reference Mean
reference_mean.description: Mean reference outcome (baseline steady state or factual forecast).

ScenarioResult.title: ScenarioResult
ScenarioResult.description: Computed outputs reference the evaluation that fixes their query and posterior.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: 'baseline' starts from the population baseline steady state (an interventional, rung-2 query). 'abducted' conditions on the individual's observed evidence and starts from the recovered fitted latent state (a counterfactual, rung-3 query).

time_index.title: Time Index
time_index.description: Abducted start only: observed fitted-state index to begin from. Defaults to the final retained fitted latent state.

time.title: Time
time.description: Abducted start only: ISO-8601 observed timestamp matching a retained fitted latent state. Use either time_index or time, not both.

ScenarioStartInput.title: ScenarioStartInput
ScenarioStartInput.description: Where the forward rollout begins (replaces the rung-2/rung-3 split).

ScientificOnlyConstruct.title: ScientificOnlyConstruct
ScientificOnlyConstruct.description: A scientific-only declaration excludes an identified construct from executable states.

SiteKind.title: SiteKind
SiteKind.description: Semantic role for each sample site.

SourceValidity.title: SourceValidity
SourceValidity.description: Source validity records whether a fact still matches its pinned inputs.

StartEpisodeResponse.title: StartEpisodeResponse
StartEpisodeResponse.description: Starting an episode returns its current status and any question-write outcome.

StateEquation.title: StateEquation
StateEquation.description: A continuous-time state equation rendered from declared scientific mechanisms.

likelihoods.title: Likelihoods
likelihoods.description: Likelihood specifications for each observed indicator

mechanisms.title: Mechanisms
mechanisms.description: Explicit state and edge dynamics; coefficients reference parameter IDs.

initialization_policy.description: Whether dynamic-state initial conditions are stationary-derived or free

observation_intercept_policy.description: Whether eligible manifest intercepts remain free or are fixed

StatisticalModelSpec.title: StatisticalModelSpec
StatisticalModelSpec.description:
A statistical model specification defines likelihoods, parameter roles, and estimation
policies.

StatisticalModelSpecArtifact.title: StatisticalModelSpecArtifact
StatisticalModelSpecArtifact.description:
This artifact combines the statistical specification with prior proposals and admission
diagnostics.

StatisticalModelSpecData.title: StatisticalModelSpecData
StatisticalModelSpecData.description: A specification with observed likelihood diagnostics from its pinned inputs.

StructuralDisposition.title: StructuralDisposition
StructuralDisposition.description:
A structural disposition classifies how compilation uses or excludes an authored model
entity.

StructuralEdge.title: StructuralEdge
StructuralEdge.description: A structural edge connects retained states or known inputs in the executable model.

StructuralInducedDependency.title: StructuralInducedDependency
StructuralInducedDependency.description:
An induced dependency records dependence created by projecting explicit latent root
confounders.

StructuralItemDisposition.title: StructuralItemDisposition
StructuralItemDisposition.description:
An item disposition explains the compilation decision for one identified authored
entity.

StructuralKnownInput.title: StructuralKnownInput
StructuralKnownInput.description:
A structural known input binds an observed indicator to a driver of the executable
dynamics.

StructuralPlan.title: StructuralPlan
StructuralPlan.description:
A structural plan translates the scientific causal design into the topology used by
model compilation.

StructuralSemanticCatalog.title: StructuralSemanticCatalog
StructuralSemanticCatalog.description:
The semantic catalog preserves authored definitions under the IDs used by the executable
plan.

TemporalEffect.title: TemporalEffect
TemporalEffect.description: A temporal effect summarizes a trajectory at requested horizons and its absolute peak.

TemporalStatus.title: TemporalStatus
TemporalStatus.description: Temporal status states whether a construct varies within the individual over time.

TimelineResponse.title: TimelineResponse
TimelineResponse.description: Typed transition journal returned by the episode read plane.

TraceChain.title: TraceChain
TraceChain.description: A trace chain stores a thinned sequence of parameter draws from one sampling chain.

TraceData.title: TraceData
TraceData.description: Trace data groups a parameter's sampled paths across chains for visual inspection.

TraceMessage.title: TraceMessage
TraceMessage.description:
A trace message records one conversational step, including any reasoning or tool
interaction.

TraceUsage.title: TraceUsage
TraceUsage.description: Trace usage records the input, output, and reasoning tokens consumed by a conversation.

TransitionRecord.title: TransitionRecord
TransitionRecord.description:
One journaled transition attempt — applied, rejected, or raised.

Rejections are recorded deliberately (a Temporal validator rejection
leaves no trace in event history). Current state is reconstructed by
replaying applied effects, not serialized into transition records.

TransitionTraceIndex.title: TransitionTraceIndex
TransitionTraceIndex.description: Promoted traces of the applied transition that produced an artifact version.

TreatmentEffect.title: TreatmentEffect
TreatmentEffect.description:
A treatment effect stores posterior effect draws and optional temporal or observed-scale
summaries.

UncheckedJsonObject.description: An unchecked JSON object carries data across a boundary before domain validation.

UploadResponse.title: UploadResponse
UploadResponse.description: An upload response identifies the stored location of an accepted data upload.

ValidationIssue.title: ValidationIssue
ValidationIssue.description:
A validation issue explains a data problem and its severity for an indicator or the
dataset.

ValidationReportArtifact.title: ValidationReportArtifact
ValidationReportArtifact.description:
A validation report summarizes whether extracted measurements satisfy the required data
checks.

WindowExpression.description: Deterministic support-window expression that returns one scalar per window. Use Python-like syntax over source_columns with arithmetic, comparisons, if/else, and helper functions such as any(), sum(), mean(), std(), first(), last(), count_true(), count_non_null(), lower(), contains(), and contains_any(). Use None for missing values.

WorkerStatus.title: WorkerStatus
WorkerStatus.description:
A worker status reports extraction progress, produced measurements, and any failure for
one worker.

WorkspaceEntry.title: WorkspaceEntry
WorkspaceEntry.description: A workspace entry identifies an available model workspace and its research question.

WorkspaceList.title: WorkspaceList
WorkspaceList.description: A workspace list provides the available model workspaces for client navigation.
